topic: Why reformer springs are great for rehab

slides.headline: Why reformer springs help in rehab
slides.sub: Adjustable support and adjustable challenge, all on one machine.

slides.title: Springs can assist or resist
slides.body: On a reformer, springs can make a movement harder or help you through it. That means someone early in rehab can practise a movement with support, then gradually take that support away.

slides.title: Load you can adjust in small steps
slides.body: Changing a spring changes the load in small, predictable steps. For rehab, that makes it easier to build up gradually rather than jumping from bodyweight straight to heavier gym weights.

slides.title: Lying down takes pressure off
slides.body: Many reformer exercises are done lying or seated, so you can train legs, hips and trunk without full bodyweight through a sore knee, hip or back. Useful early on, then progress to standing.

slides.title: Control through the whole range
slides.body: Springs keep tension on through the movement, including the return. Controlling that return, rather than letting the carriage snap back, builds strength and control in positions you use every day.

slides.title: Clinical Pilates is supervised
slides.body: Our Pilates team starts with an assessment, then sets springs and exercises for your goals and progresses them as you improve.

slides.headline: Curious how it would feel?
slides.body: Book a clinical Pilates assessment at Hybrid Physiotherapy. We'll talk through your goals, try a few exercises and set a starting level that suits you.

caption:
Those springs on the reformer are doing more than you think.

Springs can resist a movement or assist it. Early in rehab, that means you can practise a squat or a leg press with support, then gradually take the support away. Each spring change is a small, predictable step in load, which makes building up gradually much easier.

Many exercises are done lying or seated, so you can train legs, hips and trunk without full bodyweight through a sore knee, hip or back. And because the springs pull back, controlling the return builds strength through the whole range.

Our Pilates team starts with an assessment and adjusts things as you progress. Book online via the link in bio.

story.headline: Why rehab loves reformer springs
story.body: Springs can support or challenge a movement, so load goes up in small, predictable steps as you recover.
